## Findings
- claim-1: The alternate ar5iv full-text record states Theorem 1.2 for bigrassmannian \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and proves minimality of the first family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 68-110]
- claim-2: The supplied provider text identifies equations (8)–(10), Definition 2.1, and Lemma 2.5, but its mathematical content is visibly truncated at precisely required portions, including the valid-tuple conditions. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 143-189]
- claim-3: Lemma 4.2 imposes \(N\leq\min(j,n-r-i)\), whereas Theorem 4.4 then treats arbitrary valid tuples by a scaling argument; thus that bound is proof-only, not a theorem hypothesis. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 429-494]
- claim-4: Theorem 4.5 derives absence of the syzygy from Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 495-502]
- claim-5: The requested uncorrupted bounded excerpt containing complete equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1’s inequalities was not retrieved from the supplied provider material.
## Strategy
Use a provider distinct from the corrupted ar5iv rendering (arXiv PDF/source or publisher PDF) to obtain one continuous, hashed excerpt spanning pre-(8) through Theorem 4.5. Extract verbatim equations (8)–(10), Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.5, Lemmas 4.2–4.3, and Theorems 4.4–4.5; then separate theorem hypotheses from proof-only restrictions.

## Gaps
The requested target is **not established**. The only supplied full-text provider is the corrupted ar5iv extraction: it truncates equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1’s inequalities [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 143-189]. No alternate-provider bounded excerpt, stable locator set, or digest is supplied.

Known distinction, but incomplete without Definition 2.1: Lemma 4.2 temporarily assumes \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\), while Theorem 4.4 applies to every valid tuple via scaling [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 429-494]. The \(i=n-r\) proof reduction and the complete valid-tuple inequalities cannot be recorded exactly from corrupted text.

## Next
Retrieve and preserve the required alternate-provider excerpt before asserting the equation-level chain
\[
(8)\to(9)\to\text{Lemma 2.5/(10)}\to\text{Theorem 4.4}\to\text{Theorem 4.5}.
\]
